reading.body:
Csquare SFO1 is a 129.4 MW campus in Santa Clara qualifying for SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, and LEED certification. At typical AI training densities of 40 kW per rack, this would support roughly 3,200 racks, though the operator publishes no rack count or IT load breakdown. The 273,000 square feet of technical space is substantial for a single site.

California's published data center capacity totals 365 MW across 11 facilities reporting figures to this registry. Csquare SFO1 ranks twelfth in the state by published power, placing it just outside the top tier. The state has 103 mapped facilities overall, of which fewer than one in ten publish power specs. Most California data center capacity remains undeclared.

This campus sits in Silicon Valley, the region of highest compute density demand in the US, but its rank outside California's top ten published sites and the absence of any published IT capacity figure mean its actual role in AI scaling cannot be assessed from available data. Whether it runs training workloads, inference, or neither is not published.
